Cards show the latest value and its trend. Tap a card to open the metric detail.
Long-press any card to reorder, hide or restore cards. Changes save immediately.
The tune icon in the top bar also enters edit mode; the refresh icon re-reads health data.
A card without permission prompts you to open the Data settings and grant access.
Use Settings to change the number of columns and where the trend chart appears.
The header shows the current value and goal progress when a goal exists.
The chart shows history; statistics and the most recent records are listed below.
A source badge marks data coming from Garmin or another connected source.
Values follow the unit system chosen in Settings.
Tap Add a widget to configure it first; your launcher then asks where to place it.
Tap any placed widget in the list to edit its metrics, picture, tap action and appearance.
A widget name only helps you tell placements apart inside GarPulse; it never appears on the home screen.
For a photo launcher, set a picture on the widget and set its tap action to open GarPulse.
Sections run top to bottom: preview, name, picture, tap action, metrics and appearance.
Every change updates the preview at once and reaches the home screen after Save.
The question mark on each section explains that section in detail.
The preview follows your metric count and appearance settings in real time.
Widget size is suggested automatically; long-press the placed widget to resize it.
The name only distinguishes widgets inside GarPulse, never on the home screen.
Leave it empty for an automatic kind name plus its number; the trash icon clears it.
The picture sits behind the cards: it fills an empty widget and underlays metric cards.
Tap the empty preview or Choose to add a picture; transparency 100 percent means fully transparent.
All sliders move in one-percent steps.
Set a tap target for the whole widget or picture and, separately, for each metric cell.
A metric cell with no target opens that metric detail inside GarPulse.
With nothing chosen, tapping the background or picture does nothing; the trash icon clears a choice.
Export the app list or an app page list as a txt file to hand to an AI when picking a target.
Adding metrics updates the suggested widget size and the preview immediately.
Tap a metric row to choose the app or page it opens when tapped.
The refresh strip reads the latest health data; its animation keeps running until the read finishes.
Transparency 100 percent is fully transparent, 0 percent is fully opaque; sliders use one-percent steps.
Switches control the source badge, chart, metric labels, values and refresh strip.
Only elements that exist are listed; indented settings belong to the option above them.
Tap a colour swatch to change it; the selected swatch has an outline.
Data manages permissions; Data source chooses Health Connect, Garmin or both.
Display controls columns, chart placement, units, language and the app logo.
Export saves your accessible data to CSV or JSON.
Each section title has its own question mark with more detail.
Manage data access opens Health Connect to grant or revoke health data types.
Cards without permission prompt you to come back here.
Data stays on your device; nothing is uploaded unless you export it yourself.
Automatic reads aggregated Health Connect data, including data synced by other apps.
Garmin API needs a personal API key; priority decides which source wins when both exist.
The source badge on each card shows whether Garmin supplied the value.
Your key is never shown again; leaving the field blank keeps the saved key.
Refresh interval sets how often the widgets re-read data in the background (system may delay under Doze).
Fixed daily times refresh at the same times every day, e.g. right after waking up; leave empty to disable.
Both can be combined; each widget still refreshes immediately when you open the app.
Overview columns accepts one to ten columns.
The trend chart can sit below the value or become the card backdrop.
Units and language take effect at once; choose one of six app logos here.
To use your own photo as an entry point, set a picture on a widget and its tap action to open GarPulse.
Choose CSV or JSON and save the file wherever you like.
Only data you have granted access to is exported; nothing is sent online.
Shows the app version and the open-source repository.
The privacy note at the bottom of this page explains how data is handled.
